Overview

The FEG Innovation Hackathon 2026 is a two-day innovation challenge bringing together developers, startups, students, and creative thinkers to solve real-world digital entertainment problems.

Hosted by FEG India in partnership with T-Hub, participants will turn ideas into working prototypes, receive guidance from mentors, and present their solutions to FEG's product, engineering, and leadership teams.

ABOUT FEG INDIA

FEG India is the Hyderabad-based Global Capability Centre for Fortuna Entertainment Group, one of Central and Eastern Europe's leading omni-channel digital entertainment and interactive media groups.

Operating from Knowledge City, FEG India's technology hub supports global operations through scalable data infrastructure, AI-driven platforms, advanced analytics, and consumer-facing technology.

WHY PARTICIPATE?

  • Gain direct industry exposure by presenting your solution to FEG and T-Hub experts, senior leaders, and jury members.
  • Compete for ₹1 lakh per challenge for winners and ₹50,000 per challenge for runners-up.
  • Explore follow-on opportunities to build strong solutions further with FEG.
  • Discuss potential pilots, proof-of-concepts, and startup engagements with FEG.
  • Connect with developers, mentors, incubator networks, and startup communities.

HACKATHON EXPERIENCE

Shortlisted participants and teams will attend the two-day hackathon in person at T-Hub, Hyderabad on September 8–9, 2026.

Turn your idea into a working prototype, collaborate with your team, get guidance from mentors and technical experts, and present your solution to FEG and T-Hub.

View the FEG Hackathon Challenge Guide for detailed challenges, metrics, and guidelines.

Build bold ideas. Solve real problems. Create what's next for digital entertainment.

Themes

1. Session Quality and Session-to-Action Conversion

How might we turn more sessions into confident, informed actions and make every session more valuable to the user without pushing anyone to do more than they want to? The problem • Users open our products far more often than they act in them. A large share of sessions end in browsing. • Users open our products far more often than they act in them. A large share of sessions end in browsing. View the Challenge Guide for more details and evaluation metrics.

Digital Entertainment ExperienceRead more

2. Native App Experience

The product only exists when the app is open. Between sessions, it's invisible which is exactly when the moments users care about happen. Modern phones offer widgets, lock-screen surfaces, Live Activities, Dynamic Island, watch complications, and rich notifications; most of that canvas sits unused. Teams explore: widgets and lock-screen surfaces, Live Activities and Dynamic Island, watch complications, geolocation, one-tap shortcuts, voice search. Appeals to: native iOS and Android engineers, widget and Live Activities specialists, voice interface developers. Note: Relevance and convenience, not hyper-personalisation. Teams build a standalone demo app, not a production integration. View the Challenge Guide for more details and evaluation metrics.

Digital Entertainment ExperienceRead more

3. Game Load Time

Games currently take 6–8 seconds from tap to playable. Target is under 500 milliseconds cold load. The games are third-party packages certified, contractually fixed, cannot be modified – so the solution space is everything around the game. Teams explore: Prediction and prefetching, edge/CDN and caching strategy, progressive and perceived loading, lobby-to-game transitions, instrumenting real vs perceived load. Appeals to: Performance engineers, edge and CDN architects, caching and delivery specialists. Non-negotiable: Speed must not bypass protective steps; interstitials, session limits and age gates stay intact. View the Challenge Guide for more details and evaluation metrics.

Eligibility

All participants are eligible to register for FEG Innovation Hackathon 2026

Rules

Team Participation

  • Shortlisted teams will participate in the final hackathon as their registered team.
  • Teams must not change their registered team composition during the final hackathon unless approved by the organizers.
  • All team members must be available in person at T-Hub, Hyderabad throughout the final hackathon.

Challenge & Solution

  • Teams must build their solution based on their selected official FEG challenge statement.
  • Solutions should address the challenge meaningfully and demonstrate a working prototype by the final submission deadline.
  • Teams are expected to develop, refine, test, and prepare their solutions during the final hackathon.
  • For the Session Quality & Conversion challenge, improvements must focus on relevance and reduced friction.
  • Dark patterns, pressure-based approaches, or solutions that encourage users to act beyond their intent are not permitted.
  • Solutions must not bypass required responsible gambling, safety, age-gating, or protective measures.

Hackathon Participation

  • The final hackathon will be conducted in person at T-Hub, Hyderabad from 08–09 September 2026.
  • Teams must follow the official hackathon schedule, checkpoints, mentor sessions, and instructions provided by the organizers.
  • Mentors and technical experts will be available throughout the hackathon to provide guidance and feedback.
  • Participants are responsible for their own travel and accommodation arrangements.

Final Submission

  • Teams must submit their working prototype, pitch deck, demo, and any other required materials by the final submission deadline.
  • The submitted solution should be sufficiently complete to demonstrate its functionality and intended impact.
  • Teams must ensure that their final submission is accessible and ready for evaluation within the specified deadline.
  • Late submissions may not be considered for the final evaluation.

Evaluation & Selection

  • Final submissions will be evaluated by the FEG and T-Hub jury based on the official judging criteria.
  • The jury may consider factors including business impact, customer experience, originality, technical feasibility, product thinking, and compliance, as applicable to the selected challenge.
  • The Top 10 teams will be shortlisted for the final evaluation round.
  • The 3 winners and 3 runners-up will be selected across the three challenge tracks.
  • The jury's decision regarding the final selection and winners will be final.

Originality & Intellectual Property

  • All submitted work must be original and created by the participating team.
  • Teams must not submit plagiarized, copied, or previously submitted work as their own.
  • Teams are responsible for ensuring that they have the necessary rights and permissions for any third-party code, datasets, assets, or technologies used in their solution.
  • Participants must comply with applicable privacy, security, and responsible technology requirements while developing their solutions.

General

  • Participants must maintain professional and respectful conduct throughout the hackathon.
  • Any form of misconduct, cheating, plagiarism, harassment, or violation of the hackathon guidelines may result in disqualification.
  • Participants must follow the instructions of the organizers, mentors, venue team, and jury.
  • The organizers reserve the right to modify the schedule, guidelines, or evaluation process if required.
  • The organizers reserve the right to disqualify any team that violates the hackathon rules or provides inaccurate or misleading information.

FAQs

The final hackathon will be conducted in person at The Marvel, T-Hub, Hyderabad on 08–09 September 2026. Shortlisted teams must be present in person for the full two-day hackathon.

The hackathon has 24 hours of build time, with scheduled lunch and dinner breaks. The build clock runs until 12:00 PM on 09 September 2026.

Teams must submit their working prototype, pitch deck, and demo by 12:00 PM on 09 September. After the code freeze, no further changes can be made.

The Top 10 teams will be shortlisted based on jury ratings and evaluated by the T-Hub and FEG jury from 1:00 PM to 3:15 PM on 09 September.

There will be 3 winners and 3 runners-up, with one winner and one runner-up selected across each of the three challenge tracks. Each winner receives ₹1,00,000 and each runner-up receives ₹50,000. Strong teams may also receive an opportunity to build further with FEG India.
